title: Auto Filter
text: STPHE / Auto Filter Let recent chat choose the prompts. An Auto Filter rule pairs a chat condition with an effect. Rules run in their numbered order. Create a rule Open Auto Filter and enter a name. Choose a word, regular expression, or XML-tag condition. Set chat depth: zero means always on; a positive number checks that many recent messages. Choose Enable when triggered or Disable when triggered. Select matching prompts/folders or manually chosen targets, then Add filter. When a condition stops matching, the opposite effect applies. “Enable when triggered” disables its targets when the trigger leaves the checked chat range. An unsaved example: Specific Word = tavern, chat depth = 4. Set the effect and targets below before adding the rule. Group and order Use ＋ Group and subgroup controls to organize rules. A muted group gates all descendant rules while preserving their individual checkboxes. Grouping does not alter execution order: numbered rule order wins when effects overlap. The rule list has a + Group button and an Unfiled drop area. This capture shows the empty list before any rules are saved. Evaluation timing Rules react to supported chat events and rule edits. Re-evaluate now runs them manually. The master Disable all filters switch pauses automatic effects without deleting rules. Option Meaning Generation finishes or is aborted Rechecks after completion, failure, or stop. Enabled by default. Before sending (wait for filters) Includes the new user message and awaits filter effects before request assembly. Works with Send and Enter; disabled by default. The master switch and two independent send/abort checkboxes control when rules run. Before sending is unchecked by default. Example: a location trigger Create a rule matching the word tavern in the last four messages. Set its effect to enable a manually selected atmosphere prompt. The prompt becomes active while that word is in range and turns off when it no longer matches. Keep an unrelated base instruction outside this rule’s targets. Choose Enable when triggered and Manually chosen prompts/folders, then check your atmosphere prompt. No targets are checked in this unsaved example. Check your rule Use a small selection first. Test a matching message and a non-matching message, inspect native prompt states, and check overlapping rules. Local OpenAI-compatible mock tests covered streaming, non-streaming, abort/error recovery, group gating, and pre-send timing; real providers can differ. Use Re-evaluate now below the rule list to test the current rules, then inspect their target states in the prompt hierarchy.

title: Import, export & removal
text: STPHE / Import, export & removal Keep a recoverable copy. Use the Import / Export toolbar menu to transfer a hierarchy or make a backup before reorganizing it. Export A full export includes folder assignments, order, intended states, exclusions, saved filter presets, Auto Filter rules, and their groups. Native prompt definitions and active order are bundled when available. Folder and prompt context menus offer smaller exports. The Import / Export menu offers Export folder structure at the top. Individual prompt exports are also available from their More actions menu. Replace or append Replace replaces folder organization. Append adds missing organization while retaining existing local choices. Import append after an entry places imported content alongside the selected entry. Read each confirmation, especially when restoring prompt definitions. Choose Import (replace current folders) for replacement, or Import append to merge into the existing structure. Name conflicts If imported and existing prompts share a name but differ in content, the conflict dialog offers choices such as keep previous, keep both, or replace. Inspect the scope before choosing a replacement. Decision diagram for a name conflict: keep the existing prompt, keep both versions, or replace with the imported content. Removal choices Action Result Delete folder only Keeps prompts and moves them up. Remove from list Keeps native definitions, which can be inserted again. Delete permanently Removes definitions and their native order references. Export first if recovery matters. A prompt’s Delete submenu distinguishes removal from the list from permanent deletion of the definition. Older backups The internal prompt_folders settings key and prompt-folders export marker remain unchanged so renaming the extension does not strand your data. Compatibility diagram: the display name changed, while the internal settings key and backup marker stayed the same.

Documentation inspiration The guide-oriented navigation is inspired by SillyTavern’s documentation . The writing, styling, and extension screenshots here are specific to STPHE.

title: Folders & prompts
text: STPHE / Folders & prompts Organize without losing intent. Folders group prompts visually while keeping SillyTavern’s native prompt list in sync. Mute versus force all Control Behavior Folder toggle Mutes the folder and descendants. Restoring it preserves each prompt’s intended on/off state. Enable all Sets every prompt in the folder and descendants on; clears overlapping folder mute state. Disable all Sets every prompt in the folder and descendants off; clears overlapping folder mute state. Prompt toggle Changes that prompt’s intended state. A muted ancestor still prevents it from being active. The folder row has a mute toggle followed by Enable all (check) and Disable all (cross). Each prompt has its own toggle below. Read the toggle colors On: intended enabled state. Off: disabled prompt or muted folder. Gray suppression: intended on, but a containing folder is muted. Yellow mixed state: a folder contains both intended on and intended off prompts. The enabled count describes intended states. A separate “currently active” count appears when folder mutes suppress some of them. Close-up from the nested-folder test: green folder toggles, a yellow mixed Unfiled bucket, and gray prompt toggles below a muted branch. Example: restoring a mixed folder Suppose a folder contains three prompts: two enabled and one disabled. Muting the folder makes all three inactive in SillyTavern, but keeps the remembered two-on/one-off selection. Restoring the folder activates the original two prompts. Use Enable all only when you want to change the disabled prompt as well. Behavior diagram: mute and restore preserve the two-on, one-off selection; Enable all deliberately changes it. Nested folders A child folder can be muted independently. Turning its parent off and back on does not erase that child mute. Unfiled is a separate bucket, not a master switch for all named folders. Indentation shows PF Stress Test → Branch 00 → Section. Each level has its own toggle; the small triangle collapses that branch. Edit and preview Use the eye control for a read-only preview and the edit control for SillyTavern’s native editor. Save in the native editor to update the prompt. Full Preview combines enabled prompt content for inspection; it is not a guarantee of the complete provider-specific request. On each prompt row, the eye opens a read-only view and the pencil opens the native editor. Full Preview is in the toolbar. Move and reorder Use move selectors or drag and drop. Ctrl/Cmd-click selects multiple entries. Moving a selected parent includes its descendants. The native prompt order follows the tree’s top-to-bottom order. The dropdown at the far right moves a prompt to a folder. Rows can also be dragged into tree order. When loading ends STPHE serializes native changes, verifies requested states, updates the tree, and waits for its paint before releasing the loading overlay. There is no fixed completion delay. Large native context calculations can still take time. Behavior diagram: native changes are applied and verified before the updated tree is painted and unlocked.

title: Getting started
text: STPHE / Getting started Start with a small hierarchy. STPHE runs inside SillyTavern. Use a Chat Completion API to access the native Prompt Manager it organizes. Install In SillyTavern, open Extensions → Install extension and use https://github.com/miputra/STPHE . You can also obtain the files from the STPHE repository for a manual installation. For manual installation, place the extension directory in your SillyTavern user’s extensions directory. Keep manifest.json , index.js , style.css , and src/ together. Reload SillyTavern and enable the extension if it is disabled. Choose Chat Completion and open AI Response Configuration once. The STPHE panel reads the native prompt list. Upgrading from Prompt Folders? Update the existing installation. Do not install a second copy alongside it. The internal settings key and existing folder path may retain the old name intentionally. Installation diagram: install one copy, keep its files together, then open the native Prompt Manager. Create your first folder Click Folder in the floating panel and enter a name. Use a prompt’s move selector to assign it to that folder. Open the folder’s More actions menu to add a subfolder. Toggle the folder off, then on. Its prompts keep their individual intended states. Start with Folder in the top toolbar. After creating it, use a prompt row’s folder selector to move a prompt inside. Arrange the panel Drag the header to move the panel. Use grow/shrink controls, resize handles, the side-switch control, and minimize/restore to fit your layout. Search filters prompts by name or identifier. Drag the STPHE header to reposition the panel. The top-right controls grow, shrink, switch sides and minimize it. Compatibility The current integration was checked with SillyTavern 1.18.0. Native Prompt Manager methods can change between versions. If the list is unavailable, open AI Response Configuration and press Refresh. A live API connection is needed for generation, but not for basic folder organization. Refresh, at the left of the toolbar, reads the native list again after AI Response Configuration has been opened.

title: Overview
text: STPHE / Overview What is STPHE? Silly-Tavern-Prompt-Hierarchy-Expanded — STPHE — brings folders, reusable filter presets, and automatic prompt control to SillyTavern’s Chat Completion Prompt Manager. Get started → Explore folders Inside the extension Focused hierarchy from the real-app nested-folder test. Indentation shows parent and child folders; each row has its own controls. The chat page is cropped out. 01 / Organize Build a prompt hierarchy Keep large prompt collections in folders and nested subfolders. 02 / Reuse Group your filter presets Save matching rules and organize them into their own hierarchy. 03 / Automate Respond to the conversation Enable or disable prompts when recent chat meets a condition. What STPHE controls The floating panel organizes the prompts in the current Chat Completion preset. Changes apply to SillyTavern’s native prompt states and order. It does not provide an AI model or API service. Prompt rows expose their own toggle, exclusions, view/edit controls and folder selector. About the project Created by miputra . Formerly named Prompt Folders. Existing settings and exports remain compatible. Made with Claude 4.6 Sonnet, ChatGPT 5.6 Sol, and ChatGPT 6 ASTRA. The former Prompt Folders name remains in internal settings and exports for compatibility.

title: Filter presets
text: STPHE / Filter presets Save a match. Give it a home. Filter Presets are reusable manual actions. Their groups organize the saved presets themselves, independently of prompt folders. When should I use a preset? Use a saved preset when you often repeat the same matching action, such as disabling prompts containing a particular XML tag. The preset stores the search and target, not a frozen list of matches. If you edit prompt content later, the next run uses that new content. Use a prompt folder to organize the prompts themselves. Use a preset group to organize the saved actions. Use Auto Filter when an action should respond to the conversation without a manual click. Saved actions have their own hierarchy: this example places a preset inside a subgroup, separate from the prompt tree. Save a filter preset Open Filter from the toolbar. Select Prompt content and choose XML tag, Word, Regex, or Regex list matching. Enter a match and choose whether it affects prompts, their last containing folder, or all containing folders. Enter a preset name and click Save. Applying the match first is optional. Choose the source and match type, select a prompt/folder target, then name the preset and press Save. Group saved presets Scroll to Filter presets and click ＋ Preset group . Enter a name and save the group. Use the group’s ＋ control to create a subgroup. Move a preset with its group selector or drag it to a group. Use + Preset group to create a group, + on its row for a subgroup, and the row dropdowns to move entries. Existing test capture from before the rename. Run, lock, or mute Enable and Disable re-evaluate the saved match against current content before applying it. Locking a preset blocks its actions. Turning a group off blocks every preset below it without changing their individual locks. Turning the group back on restores access to unlocked presets. Groups can collapse, move, rename, and nest. Deleting a group keeps its presets and moves them up. Grouping does not execute a preset automatically. The preset row contains its lock and action controls. The parent group’s On control gates access without changing that lock. Chat filter presets Choose Chat in Match against to save a recent-chat condition plus a prompt/folder selection. Chat filter presets have their own groups. Their manual Enable/Disable controls check the condition and selection again when used. For automatic execution, use Auto Filter. Chat mode adds a recent-message depth and Check chat button. Prompt selection is a separate section below the condition. Exclusions The filter exclusion control on a prompt or folder removes it from manual content matching and saved filter presets. Auto Filter has a separate exclusion control. The funnel excludes a prompt from manual filters. The adjacent wand is a separate exclusion for Auto Filter.

title: GitHub Pages
text: STPHE / GitHub Pages Publish these docs from the repository. The documentation is a static site. It needs no package install or external theme service. Repository setup Push the extension repository, including docs/ and .github/workflows/pages.yml , to GitHub. Open Settings → Pages and select GitHub Actions as the source. Push documentation changes to main or master , or manually run the Deploy documentation workflow. Use the Pages URL shown by the successful deployment. The workflow uploads only docs/ . Project-site paths work because navigation and asset URLs are relative. Publishing diagram: the repository workflow uploads docs/ to GitHub Pages. Maintain the docs Edit the HTML pages in docs/ and shared assets in docs/assets/ . Update search-index.json when changing article content. Keep screenshots free of private prompts, credentials, and account details. Maintenance diagram: edit guide HTML, shared assets and the search index together. Preview locally python -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory docs Visit http://127.0.0.1:8765/ . Stop the preview when finished. Local preview diagram: serve docs/, open the local URL, inspect the result and stop the server. Hosting reference GitHub’s custom Pages workflow documentation explains environment permissions and publication settings. Use the linked GitHub reference for the workflow and Pages configuration shown in this diagram.

title: Troubleshooting
text: STPHE / Troubleshooting Find the state that disagrees. The panel or prompt list is missing Confirm the extension is enabled, select Chat Completion, open AI Response Configuration, and press Refresh. Reload after updating extension files. Keep only one installation of STPHE / Prompt Folders. After opening AI Response Configuration, use Refresh in the STPHE toolbar to read the native prompt list. Large folders feel slow Loading should remain active until native verification and the tree paint finish. STPHE patches value changes in existing rows rather than rebuilding every selector. Context calculation and the native Prompt Manager can still be expensive. The 500-prompt test took roughly 2.7 seconds per toggle including browser-tool overhead; this is not a speed guarantee. Check which stage is waiting: applying native changes, verifying them, or painting the updated hierarchy. A saved name looks stale Save in the native editor, then check both lists. Current STPHE reads the updated native model and observes native text/list changes. If an older copy remains loaded, reload the page. Record your SillyTavern version and whether the native name or only the STPHE name is stale. Rename is in a prompt’s More actions menu. It opens the native editor, where the new name must be saved. Where are preset groups? Open Filter, scroll to Filter presets, then choose ＋ Preset group. Chat filter presets appear when Match against is Chat. Auto Filter has its own independent group list. Look below the preset Save controls for + Preset group. These groups organize saved actions. An Auto Filter does not run Check the master switch, rule checkbox, ancestor groups, and independent Auto Filter exclusions. Check chat depth and whether the trigger is still within that range. Use Re-evaluate now and inspect later rules that may reverse the effect. Check invalid regular expressions and whether the selected targets still exist. Start by checking Disable all filters and the evaluation triggers; then check rule/group state and target exclusions. Report a reproducible problem Include extension and SillyTavern versions, prompt/folder counts, nesting depth, reproduction steps, expected state, actual state, and a screenshot. A small sanitized export helps reproduce structural problems without sharing private prompts. Report checklist diagram: include the environment, exact reproduction and focused, sanitized evidence.
